mappings.note: The inner-to-outer filling condition (K full before L starts) is the distribution rule itself - LO-2. Not LO-5: the K capacity of two is a step in the answer, not the thing asked for, which is the ORDER of filling.
Straight definition of 'valence electrons', the first term in LO-3's list. No configuration is built (so not LO-2) and no element is classified (so not LO-5).

Definition of 'valency', the second term in LO-3's list. Shares an outcome with V44 unavoidably: LO-3 fuses six separate terms into one row, so valence electrons and valency cannot be told apart by code (see report).

PARTIAL FIT. The octet's significance is chemical stability and inertness, which no outcome in curriculum 82 states. LO-3 is cited because the eight electrons in question are valence electrons, which is the nearest the frame comes to the octet rule.
The isotope clause of LO-3, asked as a difference (same Z, different A). No table or diagram to read, so unlike O9, O16 and O22 there is no LO-5 interpretation step.

Same isotope clause as V47 asked from the other side - what all hydrogen isotopes share (one proton, Z = 1). The pair honestly shares an outcome; curriculum 82 has no code that separates a similarity from a difference.

POOR FIT. Cobalt-60 in cancer therapy is a USE of an isotope, and curriculum 82 has no outcome about applications of anything. CG5 ('draws linkages between scientific knowledge and knowledge across other curricular areas') is the only text that reaches a medical application. LO-3 is deliberately not cited: nothing about what an isotope IS is graded here, so citing it would overstate LO-3 coverage.

Twin of O23 and mapped the same: identical chemistry because the valence-electron count is identical, which is LO-3's valence-electron clause used to explain an isotope fact. Both LO-3 terms are in play, which is precisely what LO-3's six-term row cannot separate.

Why 35.5 u is fractional needs only two of LO-3's terms - 'atomic mass' and 'isotopes' - joined by abundance. No numbers are supplied or worked, which is the split from P18 and S67, where an abundance calculation or its method is graded and LO-5 comes in.
Definition of 'isobars', the last term in LO-3's list. Not LO-5: no data are supplied to classify, the definition is simply asked for.

Recall of the standard calcium-argon pair. Same code as V52 because LO-3's isobar clause is all there is; definition and worked example cannot be separated by any legal code. No LO-5 - the mass numbers are recalled, not read off supplied data.

POOR FIT, but the best of the three parmanu items for CG5: this one explicitly asks the student to relate an ancient philosophical idea to the modern atom, which is what 'draws linkages ... across other curricular areas' describes. C5.1 remains an imperfect competency - it names literature and arts - and neither of its outcomes is about anything but diagrams.

PARTIAL FIT, the fullest version of the P3 and O4 gap: cathode rays and the field-deflection reasoning are discovery evidence, which no outcome covers. LO-1 is cited because what the evidence establishes is the electron's negative charge and its being a constituent particle.

Every postulate asked for is a charge-or-position claim: tiny dense positive nucleus, nearly all the mass in it, electrons around it, the rest empty. That is LO-1 across the board, with no shells and no numbers, so no LO-2 and no LO-4.

The ONE item in the chapter where LO-28 can be cited without stretching: it says 'labelled diagrams of various atomic models, as Thomson's model', and the question says 'draw a labelled diagram of Thomson's model'. The row is still defective - the verb 'Draw' was lost to the row above and an IUPAC-symbols tail is fused on the front (see report) - so I cite it only on this exact wording. LO-1 carries the second half, the charge balance that makes the atom neutral.

POOR FIT. The justification wanted is that a charged particle in circular motion accelerates and radiates - physics that curriculum 82 never states. LO-1 supplies only the setting (a charged electron moving around the nucleus). Split from V31: V31 asks for the limitation as the defect that forced the next model and gets CG7; this asks for the mechanism.

The role asked about is entirely charge-and-position - a chargeless particle sitting in the nucleus with a proton's mass - which is LO-1. The discovery half (Chadwick, 1932) matches no outcome, the same history gap as V34.

PARTIAL FIT. The first half, why the foil must be thin, is experimental design and is covered by nothing. The second half, why a few particles come straight back, is LO-1's concentrated positive nucleus and carries most of the marks, so LO-1 alone.

LO-3 supplies the definition of 'atomic number'; the contrast is explicitly demanded 'in terms of subatomic particles' - protons alone against protons plus neutrons - which is LO-1's differentiation. Not LO-4: the two quantities are contrasted, never computed. V38 asks only the definition and so gets LO-3 alone.

The whole question is the octet cap set against the 2n-squared capacity - LO-5's 'maximum number of electrons in a shell', with LO-2 for the shell scheme it caps. Harder than V41 and V42, which only quote or evaluate the formula; this one has the two rules in conflict. The stability reason behind the cap is, as in V46, stated by no outcome.
Valency as lose-gain-share is LO-3, and the worked examples require 2,8,1 and 2,6 to be built first, which is LO-2. Distinguished from V45, which defines valency with no element and gets LO-3 alone.

Same pair as S63, honestly: draw 2,8,2 over K, L, M (LO-2) then read valency 2 off it (LO-3). Not LO-43 - a shell diagram is not an electron dot (Lewis) structure, which is what LO-43 names. Not LO-28 either: what is drawn is one element's shells, not a labelled diagram of an atomic MODEL, which is the only clause of LO-28 I treat as citable.

The graded half is how symbols are written today - IUPAC approval and the letter rules - which is LO-6's international conventions, the same outcome as P8, V36 and V37. Dalton's pictorial symbols are history and match no outcome; I did not invent a code for them.

PARTIAL FIT. The answer turns on two of LO-1's particles by charge and position - like-charged protons packed together, neutral neutrons among them - but the binding mechanism that actually resolves the question is nuclear physics that curriculum 82 does not mention at any level.

The claim to be refuted is about METHOD - a plain mean against an abundance-weighted one - so LO-5's 'interpret data, such as atomic mass' is doing real work here, on top of LO-3's 'atomic mass' and 'isotopes'. V51 only explains why the value is fractional and stops, so it gets LO-3 alone; this is the same split as P18.
